description: In the continuous wide shot the waitress is standing behind the counter at 01:20 and within about half a second (01:20.75-01:21.5) is seated on the customer side next to the trucker. She never walks around the counter end; she effectively passes through the solid counter.

In the continuous sunrise wide shot a single waitress leans on the counter from the customer side (01:51). As she moves right she slides through the counter to the staff side, and a second identical waitress (same blue shirt, apron, hair bun) materializes at the far end of the counter at 01:52 and stays through 01:57. Nobody enters the frame.

The opening shots show a white semi tractor parked beside the diner. When the trucker leaves at 01:41, the truck outside is a dark green long-hood straight box truck with chrome stacks: a different vehicle in a different colour.

In the night interior shots (00:18-00:44) a second neon sign to the left of the OPEN sign shows malformed glyphs like 'ᴉᴉO'. In the later daytime wide shots of the same angle (00:59 onward) that second sign has vanished and only the single OPEN sign remains.
At 01:09 one mug sits in front of the trucker. At 01:12 there are two mugs, one in his hands and another beside it near the waitress. By 01:13 there is only one mug again.

The exterior establishing shot is dark pre-dawn blue, but the cut-in interior counter shot (00:10-00:18) shows bright white daylight through the left window. The next wide interior shot (00:18) is back to dark blue night outside the windows.
In the exterior establishing shot (00:00-00:09) no neon sign is visible in the windows. In the exterior frame at 00:10.167 a red neon sign suddenly appears in the right window without any transition.

Within roughly one second after rising from the customer-side stool (01:51), the waitress lunges rightward and is then walking behind the counter at the back wall (01:53) with no visible path around the counter; at the same moment a second, semi-transparent waitress figure fades in at the rear by the pass-through window and persists (01:52-01:57). Motion is discontinuous and an entity appears without any entering action.

entity: Plate of food served to the man
description: The waitress places a plate of food in front of the man at 01:09 and slides him a mug; by 01:15 she is holding the same plate again and carries it away (01:16-01:17), leaving the counter empty. The man never eats, gestures, or refuses, so the reversal of the serving action has no visible cause.

In the continuous sunlit wide shot (1:50.2 onward) there is only one waitress, who rises from a stool and leans over the counter at 1:51. At ~1:52 a second figure with identical wardrobe (light-blue uniform, white apron, hair in bun) materialises at the back-left end of the counter while the first waitress simultaneously walks behind the counter on the right; both are visible together through ~1:55, after which one fades away. No cut and no entrance explains a second identical person.

Within the single wide shot starting 1:17.6, the waitress stands behind the counter (service side) facing the trucker at 1:20-1:21.0. By 1:21.25 she is on the customer side directly beside him, with legs visible on the stool side, having passed through the counter in ~0.25 s with no path around it. She then also reads noticeably smaller/childlike in scale next to him (1:22-1:26) compared with her earlier standing size.

At 0:27 in the same wide camera setup the trucker sits on a stool on the customer side at the counter curve, facing screen-right toward the waitress. After the food inserts, the 0:36.5 wide shot shows him at a different spot further right, facing straight to camera with his torso on the service side of the counter and his legs on the stool side, i.e., straddling/inside the counter where the waitress had stood; the stools beside him are empty. His position and facing change without visible movement and the new placement is physically implausible.

At 1:50.167 the waitress is standing at a booth window (ketchup/mustard on the table) looking down, with the trucker still at his truck outside; at the 1:50.208 cut she is instead seated on a counter stool across the room with a mug, with no intervening shot to cover the move. Possible intended time-skip, but the cut gives no cue of elapsed time.

Seated on a stool on the customer side, she stands, leans over the counter, then moves right. Between ~01:52.2 and ~01:52.75 her legs and hips blur through the counter's front panel, and she ends up behind the counter, back to camera. She never walks around the end of the counter or through a gap; her lower body passes straight through the solid counter.

At 01:20.0 she stands behind the counter. By 01:20.25-01:20.75 her apron and lower body show on the customer side below the counter edge while her torso is still at the counter, and from 01:21 she sits on a stool beside the man. She does not walk around the counter end within the shot, so her body crosses through the solid counter in under a second.

entity: Two coffee mugs (man's held mug and the mug the waitress slides over)
description: At ~01:12.65 there are two separate mugs: one inside the man's grip and one the waitress pushes toward him. At ~01:12.9 they touch, and by ~01:13.15 only one mug is left, with both people's hands on it. One mug passes into the other and merges with it instead of stopping on contact.

entity: Man's right hand / mug under coffee pot
description: In the close-up, the man's hand wraps the mug and slides it under the pot (00:27.15-00:27.65). By 00:27.9 the hand rests far left on the counter, and the mug is in a new position at a much larger scale under the spout. No release or withdrawal motion appears between these frames: the hand and mug snap to new positions.

entity: coffee mugs on counter (man's mug and a second mug)
description: At 01:09 only the man's mug is on the counter; the waitress's hands are on the plate and carry no mug. By 01:10 a second white mug is standing behind the plate with no visible placement. The waitress then slides it toward the man (01:12), where it sits beside his own mug, and by 01:13 only one mug remains in his hand. Two mugs have merged into one. Dense frames at 2.5 fps from 69.2 to 73.6s show the extra mug appear and then collapse into the man's mug.

At 01:38 the hand slides a single flat bill (one visible layer) across the counter under its fingers. By 01:39, with no added bills shown, it has become a curled stack of at least three $100 bills in a different spot and a raised, bent orientation. The money count and form change during the hand-off with no visible action that adds bills.

The only vehicle parked at the diner in the opening exterior (00:00-00:10) is a white semi tractor. When the man leaves at 01:41-01:49, he walks to a dark green box truck with a long-nose cab and chrome stacks. The white tractor is never seen leaving and the green truck is never seen arriving, so the parked vehicle has changed identity.

entity: OPEN neon sign in diner front window
description: From 00:00 to 00:09 the right-hand front window shows a dark rectangular screen and no lit sign. At 00:10.167, in the same static exterior shot, a lit red OPEN neon sign is in that position and the dark screen is gone. The sign switches on, replacing the dark object, with no visible action.

entity: man's mug and plate of toast/egg
description: At 00:36-00:44.9 the man holds a mug and has a plate of toast and egg in front of him. In the next shot (00:44.958-00:51) he sits at the counter with only condiments (ketchup, shakers) in front of him; the mug and plate are gone, with no visible removal.

entity: Man seated at counter vs counter top / front panel
description: In the master wide shot (00:36-00:44) the man faces the camera with the counter top in front of his torso, and his mug and plate sit on the near edge, so his upper body is on the far side of the counter. Yet his jeans and legs show in front of the counter's front panel, on the aisle side below the counter top. His body sits on both sides of the solid counter at once. It also contradicts 00:24-00:27, where he sat on an aisle-side stool facing right toward the waitress, and no stool is under him here.

entity: Waitress walking from stool to back-bar vs counter
description: At 01:51 the waitress stands on the aisle side by the stools. At 01:52 her torso is behind the counter top at the back-bar coffee machine (service side), while her trailing leg shows in front of the counter's front panel on the aisle side. There is no gap or flap there. She crosses through the solid counter instead of going around its end.

entity: Man's seat position in reverse angle vs master shot
description: In the reverse from behind the service counter (00:44.958-00:51), the man sits on the far side of a short counter next to the fridges, with the stools on the opposite (near) side, and he faces this camera. In the opposing master shot just before (00:36-00:44) he also faces the camera, which looks the other way down the room. One seated man cannot face both opposite cameras. His position on the non-stool side also conflicts with the stool-side seating set up at 00:25-00:27. The counter here is a short peninsula ending at fridges and an EXIT door, not the long curved counter running to the pass-through in the master.

entity: Man and waitress seated side by side (reverse two-shot)
description: In the master (01:21-01:26) the waitress sits on the stool beyond the man, deeper toward the pass-through. The 01:26.792 two-shot looks back at them from across the counter. Their order along the counter should therefore put the man frame-left and the waitress frame-right. Instead the waitress is frame-left and the man frame-right, a mirrored seating order.

From the first interior master (00:18.708) onward, the OPEN-sign window shows a gabled building just outside, and the left windows show parked cars. The exterior establishing shot (00:00-00:10) shows the diner alone on a flat open lot with only a distant tree line and a single truck to its left. At 01:41 a side window looks onto an empty field. The view through the windows does not match the exterior that was established.

Before stirring the bowl holds roughly 3 yellow, 3 green and 3-4 red balls (clear at 01.00 and 04.50). By 09.25 no yellow ball is visible and ~4-5 red and ~4 green appear; at 09.50 about 5-6 red, 1 yellow and 1 green are visible. Yellow balls vanish and red balls multiply without any ball being added or removed from the bowl.

During stirring the hard glossy spheres become lumpy, squashed and blob-like (e.g. irregular yellow lumps at 06.00, misshapen red/green blobs at 08.50-09.75, green ball melting into adjacent shapes at 09.25) in ways beyond motion blur; rigid plastic balls should stay spherical.
The stirring right hand smears and merges with the balls; at 09.00-09.25 fingers are indistinct and appear to blend into ball shapes, giving an implausible hand-object merge.

From about 00:07 to 00:09.75 balls on the side of the bowl away from the child's stirring fingers (e.g. upper-right yellow/red/green balls at 00:07.75, 00:08.25, 00:08.50, 00:09.25) show strong motion blur and swap positions/colors between consecutive frames, jumping rather than rolling continuously. The toddler's slow single-hand stir does not appear to contact them, so their agitation is out of proportion to the cause and the motion lacks temporal continuity.

entity: balls inside bowl (yellow at 08:25, green at 08:50, red at 09:25)
description: During stirring, individual balls sit suspended in open space at mid-height of the bowl just below the left hand's fingertips (yellow at 08:25, green at 08:50, red at 09:25), not touching the fingers, glass wall, or other balls, and they appear in similar hovering positions across consecutive frames rather than as a brief bounce arc. The stirring right hand is not in contact with them.

While the right hand stirs, fingers and balls blend into each other: at 09:00 and 09:25 fingertips merge into the red and green balls with no clear occlusion boundary, and at 09:75 the index finger appears to pass into the green ball. Heavy motion blur makes this partly ambiguous.

entity: red ball held by right hand
description: As the red ball is lowered back into the bowl, it looks semi-transparent and partly merged with the right hand's fingers instead of being cleanly occluded by them or occluding them.

At 00:00 the bowl holds exactly 2 red balls (plus 3 yellow, 3 green). By 00:00.75-00:01.00 the child is holding a red ball above the bowl while both original red balls are still visible in the bowl in the same positions, and all 8 original balls are still present. A third red ball appeared with no visible source (nothing was taken from the table or elsewhere).

At 00:05.25 about 8-9 balls are visible in the bowl; at 00:05.75 only ~5 are visible (green, 2 yellow, green, one red under the fingertips) although the hand covers only a small region and no ball is seen leaving the bowl. Several balls vanish during the stir.

The starting set is ~3 red, 3 yellow, 3 green. During stirring from ~00:07.50 to 00:09.75 the red count grows to ~4-5 visible while yellow drops to ~1 and green to 1-2; nothing is added or removed from the bowl. Balls appear to change color or turn into other balls.

From ~00:07.00 through 00:09.75 the rigid spheres become blobby, elongated and smeared together (e.g., 00:09.00 and 00:09.25 show balls stretched into irregular lumps and merging), which goes beyond normal motion blur.

entity: stirring hand vs balls inside bowl
description: During fast stirring (00:08.75-00:09.75), several balls inside the bowl, e.g. the green and red balls at right-center in frames 00:09.000 and 00:09.750, render solidly over fingertips that should be in front of or around them, and occlusion edges between fingers and balls flicker. Heavy motion blur makes this ambiguous: the hand may just be blurred and semi-transparent.

entity: mirror reflection of dancer's raised right arm
description: During the first side-to-overhead arm raise, the reflected arm trails the real arm: at ~0:00.50 the real arm is horizontal while the reflected arm still angles downward; at ~0:01.25 the real arm is raised ~45-60 deg while the reflection is roughly horizontal; at ~0:01.50 the real arm is near vertical while the reflection is ~45 deg. The reflection reaches the matching pose only ~0.125-0.25 s later (synced by ~0:01.75). A mirror image cannot lag its source; perspective may account for part of the angle difference, so the lag is suggestive rather than certain.

The man appears to work at the door with both hands at mid-panel height, like turning or unlocking something, but there is no knob, lock, latch or handle there. The only doorknob is at the bottom-left of the door, well below his hands. He seems to be operating a mechanism that isn't there, and this lasts through to the end of the clip.

As he turns, his hair suddenly looks fuller and taller, with more of a pompadour, than the flat slicked style he has in the first 7 seconds. His face shape also shifts slightly. This may be caused by motion or the change in angle.

Starting ~00:08.5 the man swings his arm forward toward the door, but from ~00:08.75 to the end of the clip (00:10.0) both hands just hover and fidget in front of the door panel at chest/waist height, above the doorknob, without grasping the knob, knocking, or producing any door movement. The initiated reach neither completes nor clearly stops; it may simply be truncated by the clip end.

During the continuous head turn at ~07.0-07.25s the character's hairstyle morphs from a neat, relatively flat side part (seen 00:00-06:75) into a markedly taller, swept-back pompadour, and his facial structure (jaw width, nose/brow shape) changes so he reads as a slightly different person; no cut or hand movement to the hair explains the change, and the altered look persists in the following profile shots.

After walking to the door, both hands are raised to mid-panel height and make fiddling/gripping motions (fingers curled, one hand cupped over the other) as if operating a lock or handle, but there is no handle, lock, key or other object at that location—the only knob is far below at the bottom-left. The hands appear to work on empty air or on flat panel with no resulting effect, i.e. a grip/manipulation pose without a visible contacted object. Preceded at 00:08.50-00:08.60 by a smeared, partially doubled hand as the arm rises.

At 00:00 she wears an open V-neck blue cardigan with a white camisole clearly visible underneath. By 00:03.0-00:03.25 the front shows a high crew-neck fitted blue top with no V opening and no white layer. The garment changes type with no cut and no action that would explain it.

The framed print on the hallway wall at 00:00 shows a blue flower with a small figure on top. From about 00:01.5 it shows a person (a man in a suit) holding or merging with a large blue flower. The artwork content changes as the camera moves.

She walks from the kitchen down the hall into the bedroom, then out through a different bedroom door that leads straight back into a kitchen. That kitchen does not match the opening one: dark cherry cabinets and an over-range microwave at 00:09-00:09.75, against light oak cabinets, a tile backsplash and a countertop microwave at 00:00. The house geometry is impossible or inconsistent.

When the camera turns back toward the bedroom doorway at 00:07.0-00:08.25, the same blue-flower portrait print from the hallway hangs inside the bedroom, left of the door. A second landscape print with a red stripe has also appeared right of the door, where a small colourful picture hung at 00:06.5.
On entry at 00:04.5-00:04.75 there is a single wooden chair at the foot of the bed. By 00:05.25-00:05.75 there are two chairs side by side in that spot.

Her hair alternates between a loose, jaw-length highlighted bob in side views (00:00, 00:02.25-00:03.25, 00:05.75) and a pinned or twisted low updo with curled ends seen from behind (00:00.75, 00:04.0-00:04.5, 00:07.0-00:08.75). Hair length and volume are inconsistent across the walk.
The small frame on the bedroom side table shows a colourful object or still life at 00:06.0-00:06.5. At 00:07.5-00:08.75 it shows a photo of a seated person.
The face in profile at 00:03.0-00:03.25 looks noticeably older and fuller than the younger face at 00:00, with a different nose and jaw. This suggests identity drift.

Hair is a loose chin-length bob at 00:00-00:25, then from behind at 00:75-01:75 reads as a tucked/twisted low chignon with the ends pinned up, then loose bob again at 02:00-03:50 (ends falling freely to the jaw), chignon again at 04:00-04:75, loose bob at 05:00-06:50, and chignon/updo again from 07:00 to the end. Within one continuous take with no hands touching the hair, the hairstyle flickers between two different styles.

At 00:00 she wears a mid-teal V-neck button-front cardigan with a white camisole visible in the open neckline. By 03:00-03:25 (side/profile view) the same garment is a closed, high crew-neck fitted dark navy top with no opening and no camisole, and it stays a dark seamless fitted top with puffed shoulders for the rest of the take. The garment changed style and colour during one continuous shot with no undressing on screen.

entity: framed photo on bedroom side table
description: At 06.00-06.75 the framed photo on the side table between the doorway and window shows a pale yellow/blue still-life or landscape image. After the woman briefly occludes it (07.00), from 07.25 onward the same frame on the same table shows a portrait of a person in a dark suit and white shirt. No one touches the frame; its displayed image changed with no visible cause.

entity: framed artwork on bedroom wall between doorway and window
description: At 06.50-06.75 the wall frame next to the doorway is a small light frame with a compact colorful red/blue/green graphic. From 07.25 it is a noticeably larger frame containing a different green/red/blue mountain-like composition, in the same wall position. Camera motion explains a scale change but not the altered artwork and frame proportions.

The distinctive blue-flower portrait in a dark frame hung on the hallway wall (01.50-04.00). When the camera turns back toward the bedroom doorway at 07.00-08.25, an identical portrait now hangs on the bedroom's interior wall left of the doorway, so the same unique object appears in two places.

Walking out of the bedroom in one continuous shot leads directly into a kitchen with dark cherry cabinets, an over-range microwave, gas range and a window on the right wall. The established kitchen (00:00-02:00) has light-oak cabinets, a countertop microwave, brick backsplash and a range hood, and the bedroom was reached via a hallway, not directly off a kitchen. The house layout changes to a different, unmapped kitchen.

The distinctive flower-figure painting hung on the hallway wall outside the bedroom, beside the bedroom doorway (00:00-04:00). After the camera pans inside the bedroom, the same painting appears on the bedroom's interior wall to the left of the exit doorway (07:00-08:50), i.e. on the other side of the wall/room, which is incompatible with the established map.

She entered facing the headboard wall, so the entry door should be behind her; after only a ~90deg left pan (05:50-06:75) a doorway appears on the side wall next to the left window, and through it is a bright room with a paned exterior door rather than the dim hallway with the paintings she came from. The doorway she exits through does not geometrically correspond to the entry door or the hallway seen beyond it.

The middle cup holds a tall stack of gold coins through 2.5s; by 3.0s it shows only a single silver coin near the rim and later appears empty, although the hands only interact with the front-left cup.
Four cups are present from the start through ~9.0s; at 9.5-9.75s only three cups remain on the table while the man's hands hold only a coin, so one cup disappears without being removed.

entity: loose coins on beige center / table layout
description: The gold and silver coins lying in front of the cups on the beige center (clearly visible at 3-5s) are gone in later wide shots (beige area empty at 9-9.75s), and the beige center morphs from a large swirl-patterned oval to a narrow band/small circle as the camera moves.

entity: near/right hand holding coin over front cup (and far hand holding coin at rear cup)
description: After lifting coins out of the front cup at ~02:25, the right hand poises a coin at the cup rim in a dropping posture from ~02:75 and holds it there for the remaining ~7 seconds while the camera pulls back; the coin is never released. The far hand likewise holds a coin edge-on over the rear cup from 00:00 to 09:75 without ever dropping it. The 'drop coin into cup' action is set up repeatedly but never resolves, giving a looping/stalled hover rather than a completed or visibly interrupted action.

In the close 00:05-00:05.75 views he has a moustache with light stubble on the jaw. By 00:09-00:09.75 (side view) the jaw and chin beard looks noticeably fuller and darker. There is no cut, and only about 4 seconds pass. This may just be side lighting and shadow, so it is a weak signal.

entity: coin held by performer's near (right) hand against the near cup
description: From ~04.5s to ~06.75s the coin sits flat against the outside wall of the near cup, below the fingertips, as if adhered to the cup surface; only a fingertip touches its upper edge while the fingers otherwise rest on the cup rim, so the coin is not visibly gripped or pinned and appears stuck to the cup exterior while the hand moves. A similar flat coin-on-cup-wall placement appears at the far hand (05.0-06.5s).

entity: coin stack inside middle cup (cup B)
description: At 00:00 the middle cup holds a stack of embossed gold coins up to its brim. No hand touches this cup; the hand only works the front-left cup. Yet by 00:02.5 the stack sits clearly lower in the cup, and at 00:03.0 the top coin has changed from an embossed gold coin to a plain silver disc. The contents' level and identity change with no visible action.

At 00:09.0 four cups stand together on the felt (back, left-rear, front-left, front-right). From 00:09.25 to 00:09.75 only three cups are visible: back, left and front-right. Both hands are beside or above the cups and none lifts or moves one, and nothing in front of the group could hide a cup. One cup seems to vanish.

entity: four-cup arrangement on the green field
description: During the close-ups (0-4.0s) the cups form a 2-D diamond cluster with clear depth separation (back cup, centre cup, right cup, front-left cup). By ~5.0-7.5s, seen from the front, they read as an evenly spaced left-to-right row of four sitting along the performer's edge of the green field. By 9.0s, seen from the side, they are a compact cluster again. A diamond seen from the front should still show one cup clearly behind the others. A straight row seen from the side at 9.0s should recede in depth as a line. Neither happens, so the spatial layout of the cups seems to re-form to suit each viewpoint during the continuous camera move.

In the close-ups the cups sit well inside a broad green oval surrounded by the medallion ring. At ~6.0-6.25s the green field is a narrow band right at the performer's edge, and a large plain red expanse with no medallions stretches far to the right. By 7.5-9.75s the table is a small round table with a centred green oval and medallions all round. The size of the tabletop and the shape and position of the field relative to the performer do not stay geometrically compatible through the uncut pull-back.

From 00:02.25 to about 00:04.0 the foreground man runs a dark comb through his hair above his ear. In the mirror at the same moments he holds a small white blade against his eyebrow or forehead. The reflection shows a different object at a different place on the head.

entity: man's head pose and hand position vs reflection
description: The reflection often fails to match the real body. At 00:01.75 the real hand holds the tool up at the temple or eye with the head turned in profile, while the reflection holds it at the nose with the face frontal and eyes closed. Throughout the clip the real man tilts his head up in profile, but the reflection shows a near-frontal face, often looking down. Given the over-the-shoulder camera angle, the mirror cannot show these poses.

At 00:09.0 the foreground right hand is open in a pinch near the jaw with no razor visible, while the reflection presses a razor against the jaw. At 00:09.25 the real hand holds the razor upright, away from the face, while the reflection still has the blade on the cheek.

During the combing section the real man's hair looks messy and pushed up, while the reflection's hair stays neatly slicked back. Afterwards the real hair returns to its earlier neat state with no explanation.

The man shaves dry skin with no shaving cream, using a small white sliver of a tool. Midway the action jumps from shaving to combing his hair (only in the real view) and then back to shaving. The tool changes between a white plastic-looking blade, a dark comb and a silver razor.

The razor is drawn repeatedly across dry, unlathered chin, upper lip, cheeks, temple and forehead for the full 10 s, yet the stubble, skin and eyebrows show no change at any point — no hair removed, no lather displaced, no skin drag or reddening. The stroking action never produces its expected effect; the razor reads as hovering/miming rather than acting on the skin.

At 01:75 the real man's razor hand is raised to his temple/beside the eye, while the reflection shows the razor against the bridge of the nose with eyes closed and head lowered; at 04:25 the real razor is at the temple/brow while the reflection shows it at the eye/nose with face fully frontal. The reflected motion does not track the real motion that should cause it, as if the two were animated independently or out of phase.

entity: razor in real hand vs reflection
description: At 09:00 the real man's right-hand fingers are pinched together near his jaw with no razor visible, while the reflection clearly shows a razor held against the cheek; at 09:25 the razor reappears in the real hand. The reflection depicts an action/object that the real scene is not producing.

The chin-up stroke sequence from 00:00-01:50 (razor at upper lip -> chin tilt -> stroke down jaw) recurs almost pose-for-pose at 05:00-07:25 and again around 08:50-09:50, with no progression in the task (no area completed, no rinse, no change in face). The action loops rather than advancing.

From 02:25 to 04:00 the razor is dragged repeatedly across the eyebrow and forehead (no stubble there), then the hand simply returns to the chin; the eyebrow and hairline are unchanged. The action is neither completed nor visibly interrupted and produces no effect.

entity: Man - real body vs mirror reflection
description: From about 0:02.0 to 0:04.0 the real man's head is turned so his right ear and cheek profile face the camera, and his hand holds the razor in the side hairline/temple above the ear. Over the same frames the reflection shows the head bowed and facing straight out, eyes lowered, with the fist and razor pressed to the centre of the forehead/eyebrow. The reflection's head orientation and hand placement do not correspond to the body casting it, and nothing on screen explains the difference.

entity: real man's right hand / grooming tool
description: At 00:09.000 the real right hand is still in a pinch-grip pose under the jaw, but nothing is between the fingers: the tool is gone. In the mirror at the same instant, the hand holds the white tool against the cheek. The tool is back in the real hand at 00:09.250. The grip is shown as holding while there is no object in it.

entity: real man's right hand / tool vs. reflected hand / tool
description: From about 02.25 to 04.00, the real hand pushes a dark tool into the hair on the crown or top of the head. In the mirror, the hand presses a white tool flat against the forehead and brow, well below the hairline. One action cannot touch both places at once, so the real contact and the reflected contact are physically incompatible.

entity: real man's tool tip vs. face
description: In several frames the reflection shows the blade touching the skin while the real tool tip floats a few centimetres off the face: 00:00.250, where the tip is in the air in front of the jaw while the reflection is on the chin; 00:01.750, where the tool is held in the air at cheek level while the reflection is on the nose; and 00:09.250, where the tip is pointing up in front of the jaw while the reflection is on the chin. The shaving or grooming contact exists only in the reflection.

entity: real man's tool vs. reflected tool
description: At 09.750 the real tool is at the temple or eyebrow beside the eye, while in the mirror the tool rests under the nose on the moustache. The two contact locations disagree.

From about 00:02.25 to 00:04.0 the object in the real hand, pressed into the hair above the ear, appears as a dark comb-like shape. In the mirror at the same moments, the hand holds a bright white/pale bar on the forehead. Before (00:01.75) and after (00:04.25) this stretch, both views show the same pale slim tool. During the stretch the object seems to change identity or appearance with no visible swap.
